column1: # The group a camera's source puts it in (`placement.group_by: {field: source, cut_at: host}` over a url field that
# declares its schemes, `fields.source.schemes: {<scheme>: {host, fragment, none} | {}}` — {} is «by the RFC»; one
# declaration read by the url rule and the grouping alike): one table for the course (Source/, Python) and the product (Go),
# read the same way by both: Source/tests/testdata/group_of.tsv (course, tests/test_group_of_table.py) and

# testdata/group_of.tsv at the product's root (w2cplatform TestTheSharedTableOfGroups), byte for byte. Owner: «Паритет». ADR-0053 (the group is the device's host, e3fa789); decisions of «Архитектор», 2026-10-06. Seeded from the product's deviceOf (vms/gate.go), its
# tests, the course's reviews 8, 10, 13, 14 and the course's seed (7fbcbade), merged.
# source: {type: url, schemes: {rtsp: {}, http: {}, file: {}, ipint: {fragment: none}, driverpack: {host: path, none: [file]}, mirror: {host: path, fragment: none, none: [local]}}}
#   a field's schemes name only what an operator writes into the row and an actuator opens: a scheme with no actuator
#   is not declared (onvif), one with an actuator comes back with its rows here; an address a platform or a subsystem
#   builds in memory (ingest://) is no spec key. A scheme not in the field's map is refused, its host unread:
#   nosuch://10.0.0.5/ below is that case (a made-up scheme: the row is about the map, not about any one scheme).
#   the group is the source's HOST in one spelling: lowercased, without the root's trailing dot; an IP literal as netip
#   writes it — IPv6 unbracketed, zero runs folded, zone dropped; IPv4-mapped as the IPv4 address
#   the scheme and the port are no part of it: rtsp:// and ipint:// to one host, :554 and no port, are one group
#   ipint: '#' is a character, not a fragment (ipintd reads it so): the host is after the LAST '@'
#   driverpack (`host: path`): the device's address is the path's first segment; the authority is the vendor — the
#   driver, not the device — and no part of the group; with the path empty the authority serves as the host, so
#   driverpack://<vendor> is the whole vendor's group; `none: [file]`: driverpack://file/… is a file and in no group
#   `none` holds in its own scheme only: rtsp://file/x is host `file`; the authority is judged in one spelling
#   (driverpack://FILE/x is the file; driverpack://file:1/x is not, its group the path's host)
#   with `cut_at: host` declared, a host that cannot be read is a refusal (400) on both sides, never «taken, no group»
#   a host that is neither RFC 1123 labels nor an IP literal is refused: a percent-escape, '_', non-ASCII, a numeric
#   last label that is not the dotted-decimal IPv4 it looks like (010.0.0.50, 10.1, 0x0a.0.0.1)
#   an authority whose port after the host is not a number (rtsp://cam:hunter2/, rtsp://admin:pw/x@h/) is an unreadable
#   host: no group, refused (ADR-0053 as «Платформа» made it precise)
#   refusing is the url rule's business, grouping is group_by's: a source refused whose host can still be read keeps
#   the group of its host (an old row stays with its neighbours) — the row says the group AND refused; a login or a
#   password in the path of a `host: path` scheme (admin:Hunter2%40…) is the url rule's own refusal by that option
# Columns, tab-separated; a line that begins with '#' and an empty line are no row:
#   source   the camera's source as written (`mirror` is testsub2's scheme: host: path, fragment: none, none: [local])
#   group    the group; <none> — in no group (a `none` of its scheme, or refused with no host to read)
#   fault    empty — taken; bad_url — refused at the door, 400 (a word of fault.tsv; the reason in `detail`):
#            its url rules, no host (a bare path too — a file camera only through its scheme's `none`), or a host no
